edits.old: Imbalance is handled during optimization via class-weighted binary cross-entropy, with fixed weights (\texttt{normal}=1.0, \texttt{attack}=1.5). This increases the cost of attack misclassification while preserving complete coverage of normal operating behavior.
edits.new: In the initial multihead training, attack-loss weights are (\texttt{normal}=1.0, \texttt{attack}=1.5). Rebalanced fine-tuning uses inverse-frequency weights estimated from training labels: 2.5445 for normal and 0.6223 for attack. Motor cross-entropy balances the two classes on attack windows. Each phase loss assigns half its weight mass to affected labels and one quarter each to normal zeros and unaffected phases during attacks.

edits.reason: Replace unperformed threshold tuning and obsolete numbers with the selected rebalanced results
edits.old: To improve the operating point beyond the default sigmoid threshold, we apply an epoch-wise threshold tuning routine that scans decision thresholds in $[0.1,0.9]$ and selects the value maximizing validation F1. With class-weighted training, dual-stream (raw+differential) inputs, and the Bi-GRU architecture, the proposed pipeline substantially outperforms the LSTM baseline and achieves $\sim$92\% test accuracy. It remains effective for low-severity attacks, achieving $\sim$96\% detection accuracy for $(0<\alpha \le 0.001)$ (Fig.~\ref{fig:Severityeffect}).
edits.new: Attack and phase outputs use the fixed threshold 0.5. With rebalanced training, dual-stream (raw+differential) inputs, and the CNN--Bi-GRU architecture, the proposed pipeline achieves 93.46\% validation accuracy, 90.59\% balanced accuracy, 96.50\% precision, and 95.32\% attack recall. Normal-window false positives are 14.14\%; average precision is 0.9937 and ROC-AUC is 0.9758 (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve). Figure~\ref{fig:Severityeffect} evaluates detection across stored severity groups; it does not measure severity-estimation accuracy.

edits.reason: Replace the unfair historical/direct cross-dataset comparison with completed matched baselines
edits.old: To contextualize these results, we compare against an unoptimized LSTM baseline and prior PMU-based \cite{guha} and IED-based \cite{aljohani2024} approaches, as summarized in Table.~\ref{tab:comparison} While these infrastructures can reach comparable accuracies, they require higher-cost instrumentation and are less suitable for consumer-edge deployment. In contrast, our EMU-based Bi-GRU framework provides competitive performance using low-cost sensing at the PCC.
edits.new: Table~\ref{tab:comparison} compares the completed attack-only baselines with an always-attack predictor and the proposed model. LSTM, CNN--LSTM, and CNN--Bi-GRU share the same inputs, split, width 64, Adam learning rate $10^{-3}$, batch size 128, attack-loss weights 1.0/1.5, and at most 40 epochs; checkpoints maximize validation balanced accuracy at threshold 0.5. The proposed model receives additional multihead training and fine-tuning, so the comparison evaluates complete pipelines rather than architecture alone. Prior PMU-based~\cite{guha} and IED-based~\cite{aljohani2024} studies provide context because their datasets and sensing setups differ.
